key_findings: **4-slot vftable layout uniform across all Sqwt EventHandler<T,EventArgs> typed-delegate vftables.** Slot 0 = per-class dtor (varies, matches scalar-deleting-destructors cataloged later); slot 1 = SHARED FUN_0094C3A0 (Remove/list-management, 172B); slot 2 = SHARED FUN_0088AB00 (Invoke thunk, 13B); slot 3 = per-class RTTI Complete Object Locator (varies). Strong inference of universality across all 173 cataloged delegate vftables based on 3-vftable sample with identical slot 1+2 contents.

**Slot 2 (FUN_0088AB00) is the canonical bound-member-function-pointer trampoline.** 13-byte body: `(**(code **)(this + 0x28))()`. The +0x28 field is the captured method pointer set by the ctor (BCS-Y-1149/1152/1157/1158/1162/etc per capture-layout finding). Trampoline propagates all args via registers/stack natively (Ghidra emits 'Could not recover jumptable' suggesting JMP indirect rather than CALL). Confirms Sqwt delegates are the canonical C++ 'bound member function pointer + this' pattern with NO per-instance vtable customization for Invoke - the customization lives entirely in the captured method pointer.

**Slot 1 (FUN_0094C3A0) is a Remove/list-management operation** with self-destruct semantics. Operates on a buffer at this[+0x8..+0xC] (int-array start + end pointers) and a short count at this[+0x14]. Linear-search-and-splice pattern: find param_2 in the buffer, remove it via _memmove_s (unless this[+0x16]&2 set - skip-compaction mode), decrement count. If count reaches 0 AND this[+0x16]&1 set, calls slot 0 (dtor) on self via virtual call - the canonical 'self-destruct on last subscriber removed' pattern. Architecturally: this is consistent with the EventHandler<T> instance maintaining a list of either: (a) subscription channels it's registered to (for cleanup on dtor), or (b) bound subscribers if used as multicast container.

**Per-class customization in delegate vftables is minimal - just dtor + RTTI.** The shared slots 1+2 mean every EventHandler<T,EventArgs> across the 173 cataloged delegates behaves identically for Invoke + Remove. Only the destructor (which knows the owner class for vftable restoration) and the RTTI metadata differ per-class. Massive compile-time code de-duplication via template instantiation.

**Client-architecture 'Sqwt UI elements follow a uniform heap-factory' supporting evidence**. The slot-layout uniformity strengthens client-architecture 'Sqwt UI elements follow a uniform heap-factory' section's claim that the Sqwt delegate system is a uniform compile-time-generated pattern: every owner class gets a typed-delegate vftable, but the dispatch behavior (Invoke + list management) is shared boilerplate.

vftable_slot_layout.slot_0: per-class dtor (scalar deleting destructor). Per-vftable. Cataloged earlier (BCS-Y-1148/1150/1155/1156/1160/1161 etc).
vftable_slot_layout.slot_1: FUN_0094C3A0 = Remove/list-management (172B). Universal across all delegates. Cataloged as BCS-Y-1335.
vftable_slot_layout.slot_2: FUN_0088AB00 = Invoke thunk via captured method ptr (13B). Universal. Cataloged as BCS-Y-1336.
vftable_slot_layout.slot_3: Per-class RTTI Complete Object Locator pointer. Per-vftable. Not a code function.

captured_field_layout_recap.+0x20: captured target object pointer (this for the method)
captured_field_layout_recap.+0x28: captured method pointer (read by slot 2 Invoke thunk)
captured_field_layout_recap.+0x2C: captured 'extra' arg (purpose still unclear - may be MI offset, bound arg, or secondary method)
